% Define the constants in each category.
prices(45; 60; 75; 90).
winners("Alejandro"; "Faye"; "Irma"; "Phillip").
butterflies("atlas"; "emperor"; "grayling"; "peacock").

% For each winner, match with exactly one price and one butterfly.
{match(W, P, B): prices(P), butterflies(B)}=1 :- winners(W).

% No option in any category will ever be used more than once.
{W1=W2; P1=P2; B1=B2}=0 :- match(W1,P1,B1), match(W2,P2,B2), (W1,P1,B1)!=(W2,P2,B2).

% 1. Alejandro's purchase cost less than Irma's purchase.
P1<P2 :- match(W1,P1,B1), match(W2,P2,B2), W1="Alejandro", W2="Irma".

% 2. The insect that sold for $90 was either the atlas butterfly or the emperor butterfly.
{B="atlas"; B="emperor"}=1 :- match(W,P,B), P=90.

% 3. The peacock butterfly cost more than Irma's purchase.
P1>P2 :- match(W1,P1,B1), match(W2,P2,B2), B1="peacock", W2="Irma".

% 4.1 Alejandro's purchase and Irma's purchase are different.
W1!=W2 :- match(W1,P1,B1), match(W2,P2,B2), W1="Alejandro", W2="Irma".

% 4.2 Alejandro's purchase was the emperor butterfly or sold for $45.
{B="emperor"; P=45}=1 :- match(W,P,B), W="Alejandro".

% 4.3 Irma's purchase was the emperor butterfly or sold for $45.
{B="emperor"; P=45}=1 :- match(W,P,B), W="Irma".

% 5. The four butterflies were Phillip's purchase, the insect that sold for $60, the butterfly that sold for $45 and the butterfly that sold for $90.
{W="Phillip"; P=60; P=45; P=90}=1 :- match(W,P,B).

final.ground_truth:
Prices	Winners	Butterflies
$45	Alejandro	grayling
$60	Irma	emperor
$75	Phillip	peacock
$90	Faye	atlas
